# Paper and audit scope

*You give them something to eat: Dietary Diversity, Coverage, and Catholic Aid in Rwanda*. Seventh revision reviewed Reject; eighth revision in progress; all seven genuine recommendations Reject at the unchanged leading general-interest standard. Public branch codex/research. Internal self-audit follows the retained public JPE TEMPLATE.qmd criteria/MIT attribution. No journal manuscript ID, official JPE certification or independent full replication is asserted.

# Data, rights and sources

All default inputs are supplied. Corrected Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.15881329 is open CC BY 4.0; actual metadata/correction/checksum are in docs/sources/zenodo-rights.json. Withdrawn/restricted predecessor excluded. Household panel: 5,506 rows/52 numeric fields; supplementary household panel: 5,506 matching rows; child panel: 7,356 numeric rows. Arbitrary linkage keys replace source identifiers; contacts, exact geography/dates, free text and administrative lists are excluded. Field review supplements numeric checks without guaranteeing universal anonymity.

Both source extractors verify archive MD5/SHA256, exact source members and independently pinned output bytes. Altered data plus rewritten generated provenance and a corrupt source archive are rejected. Original source ZIP is ignored. Source-to-extract replication starts from corrected processed panels, not all upstream questionnaire cleaning. Codebooks distinguish inherited economic/anthropometric preprocessing, food recall/transforms and unrecovered monetary price base.

Item information identifies 1,730 endline diets; 1,728 complete modules are the initial sample. All 1,793 baseline eligibles receive interval endpoints. The one-household discrepancy from the original 1,794 is retained. Twenty smaller public CSV views reconstruct three immutable inputs byte for byte; they are aliases for inspection, not extra observations or evidence of independent execution.

# Software and execution

Python 3.12.10, NumPy 2.5.2, pandas 3.0.5, SciPy 1.18.1, Matplotlib 3.11.1; exact tested direct/transitive packages in requirements-lock.txt. Existing MiKTeX 25.12 supplies optional pdflatex. Optional extraction openpyxl 3.1.5; visual/cold-copy tools PyMuPDF/Pillow; initial independent Stata/MP 19 reference uses built-in commands. Requested optional LR prose screen is separate. No language model processes data or enters scientific estimates.

Windows 11 x64, eight available logical processors; no GPU/API/network after installation. Allow 2 GB RAM/150 MB reproduction space plus packages; physical RAM not measured. Fourth-reviewed Windows master/PDF runtime 80.47 seconds; hosted source e14eb65 master 35.46 seconds. Single command `python run.py --pdf`; omit --pdf for all numerical outputs; --from-source runs direct-ZIP reconstruction.

Master checks references, estimates initial ANCOVA, constructs conditional ratio/finite regions, solves diversified allocation and cost scenarios, accounts for child cohorts, computes ANCOVA CR2/omissions, records failed block stress tests, projects coherent distributions, examines institutional/resource-value rules, selects quota moment scales from baseline weights only, encloses a shared exponential event, verifies numerical allocation proposals, builds exhibits, runs all core and quota validators and compiles three times. Scientific paths are project relative. Initial 9,999 village multipliers and revised 99,999 block multipliers use seed 20260930; synthetic stress uses seed 20261001, 800 assignments/scenario and 4,999 diagnostic multipliers.

# Limits and classification

HDDS is household food access rather than child nutrition. The new quota allocation bound is conditional, wide, and not an impossibility theorem; it is a separate 95% event from the earlier finite constructions. Institutional/cost sensitivities remain explicitly tied to the earlier coherent region. Smaller block-region losses are explicitly exploratory. Transport needs comparable weighting, original delivery, stable proportional costs and no changed cross-village interference. Cash overhead was standardized to a separate national program of 56,127 beneficiary households for each transfer amount. Mixed-program marginal/activation costs and hard realized budgets are not observed. Cost/take-up scenarios hold effects fixed. Saving theory is illustrative and not identified mediation.
